cards.title: WiiM: a seek can briefly move the queue to the end of the item, and a stop then marks it fully played
cards.area: server / providers/wiim/player.py position guard; player_queues position jump; playback_tracker; audiobookshelf on_played
cards.summary: Follow-up from #6749 (riskywhat). After a seek on a WiiM the chapter progress briefly jumps to the end of the item; a pause or stop within a few seconds saves the end as resume point and marks the item fully played, which Audiobookshelf then marks as finished. The reporter attached two tests that fail on dev.
cards.fix: WiiM provider: keep ignoring the device's position after a seek until it reports our new stream at a position that isn't its length (position != duration; != so radio with duration 0 still shows progress). Progress stays at the 0 set by play_media until a normal reading arrives. Provider-only, no core change, no time window.
cards.checked: Opus subagent on origin/dev and backport/2.10.8 (same on stable 2.10.7, which lacks #7022). A queue seek starts a new stream at the seek point (player_queues/controller.py:959-983) whose length the WiiM is told is the remaining time (helpers/upnp.py:214). For ~0.5 s after taking it, the WiiM reports STOPPED with position = that full length; wiim/player.py:595-596 lifts the old-position guard as soon as the new URI shows, :598-600 adopts the position, and the state stays PLAYING (LOADING maps to PLAYING, :42-47). The position-jump handler (controller.py:1417-1455) adds the seek offset, so the queue lands at the end; #7022's check (:1428-1430) only skips stopped/idle players. A stop then saves the end (:2078-2080) and playback_tracker reports it fully played (:686-693, 752), reaching Audiobookshelf via on_played is_finished (audiobookshelf/__init__.py:1276-1406). Reporter's tests: 3 pass, 3 fail on dev and backport/2.10.8. Code-only repro. Fix A/B: the new WiiM test fails without the fix (1080 == 0) and passes with it; wiim 223 passed, wiim + related queue tests 252 passed, no existing test changed; cherry-picks cleanly onto origin/stable (221 wiim tests pass). Opus + GPT Sol self-review clean. The reporter's queue tests feed a PLAYING 1080 straight into the queue, so they only pass with a core guard, which the fix-at-source rule rules out.
cards.plan: Local fix (code-only repro): release the WiiM guard only when the new stream's position is below its duration. Marvin tests on a WiiM, then PR with backport (Audiobookshelf books marked finished).
cards.reply:

After a seek the WiiM briefly reports the full length of the new stream, and Music Assistant takes that over as soon as it sees the new stream. I'm making the WiiM provider ignore that position until the device really plays from the new start, so the queue and Audiobookshelf no longer see the end of the book.

cards.title: Sonos Port: native playback fails with ERROR_PLAYBACK_NO_CONTENT, AirPlay volume snaps back
cards.area: server / providers/sonos player.py _on_playback_error, streams controller (port 8097); airplay/player.py volume (with #6664)
cards.summary: 2.10.7 HA add-on, Sonos Port 'Office' (line-out Variable). Native playback fails at once ('Speaker Office could not play None and reported ERROR_PLAYBACK_NO_CONTENT'), with MP3 and radio, Flow mode on and off, publish IP auto or the HA LAN IP. On AirPlay it plays, but volume changes from MA or the Sonos app snap back after a few seconds until MA clears the AirPlay output. Same error as the bot-closed support#5721.
cards.checked: Opus subagent, 2.10.7 = dev on these paths. 'None' is the speaker's own trackName/itemId in the playbackError event (player.py:1028-1034 on 2.10.7), so it failed before resolving any item; no httpStatus, so most likely no HTTP answer from MA. Flow on (play_stream_url) and off (play_cloud_queue) both need the Port to fetch http://<publish_ip>:8097; Sonos app, AirPlay and the browser don't, so likely a reachability problem (VLAN/firewall/port 8097), about 65%. Volume: Port on Variable has VOLUME_SET, so __control_for_output returns NATIVE and owns_volume is False (same as #6664); the Sonos provider doesn't push volume back. MA-side snap-back candidates: AirPlay DACP device-volume > update_volume_from_device > _adopt_device_volume writes VOLUME= back without an owns_volume check (airplay/provider.py:1111-1135, airplay/player.py:828-839, 1031-1044), or _enforce_volume_limits if a min/max volume is set (players/controller.py:2150).
cards.plan: Need a Verbose SONOS + AirPlay + Streams log of one native start and one AirPlay volume change, the diagnostics, the network layout and any min/max volume. No 'Cloud Queue request' line = network; itemWindow items=0 = MA bug.

cards.area: server / controllers/player_queues _handle_play, players cmd_play (stable) + providers/bose_soundtouch player.py
cards.summary: Docker, Bose SoundTouch speakers, local/Tidal. On 2.10.5 pause+resume played 2-3 s then went silent. fmunkes' server#6821 (merged 10-10, on 2.10.7) makes MA stop instead of pause while it streams to a SoundTouch; OzGav closed the issue. On 2.10.7 (10-17) pause now stops, but play/pause again doesn't restart at all, no ffmpeg. Phone ('This device') resumes fine. You reopened it 10-21 10:01 UTC.
cards.fix: server#6607 (dev, merged 09-30, in the 2.11 beta, not on stable): has_lost_paused_stream() makes _handle_play and cmd_play resume the queue from the saved position when a PAUSED player's queue session was cleared by a stop.
cards.checked: Opus subagent on origin/stable (2.10.7) and dev. #6821 drops PAUSE while streaming over UPnP (bose_soundtouch/player.py:619-631), so core sends Key.STOP (:227) and tears down the stream session (on 2.10.7 as 0f281c869f). The speaker then most likely reports PAUSE_STATE with source UPNP, so the player shows PAUSED (:609). UI play_pause goes to player_queues _handle_play: queue PAUSED, so it calls the speaker's play() (stable controller.py:1909-1918), which only presses Key.PLAY (:210); no stream left, nothing plays. HA play takes players/cmd/play (:699) to the same player.play() fallback (:4956). Diagnostics: no errors, no streams, 15 idle queues and 1 paused. server#6607 on dev covers this case (player_queues :327, :2100; players :682). Reproducible without hardware: stub the SoundTouch client in tests/providers/bose_soundtouch/test_player.py and feed PAUSE_STATE/UPNP after a stop. Medium-high confidence; the PAUSE_STATE report is inferred, not seen.

cards.title: Google Home speakers don't resume a voice-started radio station after an announcement
cards.summary: 2.10.7 HA add-on, several Google Home minis and a Hub. Radio started by voice on the speaker ('play radio station X', so Google's own Cast app plays it), then music_assistant.play_announcement: the announcement plays, the radio doesn't come back. Log: 'restoring the previous state failed: Can not resolve stream URL: Invalid PlayerMedia data'.
cards.checked: Code read on origin/dev (same on stable). A foreign Cast app becomes a passive source without play/pause (chromecast/player.py:794-815) and current_media is just its content_id (:751). After the announcement, _restore_after_announcement calls _handle_cmd_resume (announcements.py), which finds no MA queue, a passive source it can't select, and falls back to player.play_media(prev_media) (controller.py:4187-4190). That media has no queue session or source id, so the stream controller raises 'Invalid PlayerMedia data' (streams/controller.py:741-751). MA's announcement also replaced Google's receiver app, so there is nothing left to resume. Reporter confirmed the voice start, so the foreign-app assumption is theirs, not a guess. Not reproduced live: no unattended way to start Google Assistant radio on a Cast speaker.
cards.plan: Design call (row #6837). Reply explains it and gives the workaround: start the station from MA.

cards.summary: 2.10.7 HA add-on on HA 2026.10.2 (also 2026.10.1). After an HA core restart the Home Assistant plugin goes into error and stays there. Repair and Reload both fail with 'Command hass/search_control_entities is already registered', only an MA add-on restart clears it. The post-connect block (:291-303) already handles CancelledError. cards.title: FLAC flow stream holds back audio on quiet passages; HEOS stops and can't resume
cards.area: server / controllers/streams/controller.py flow route chunk_size, helpers/ffmpeg.py, helpers/process.py
cards.summary: Docker 2.11.0.dev2026100703, native HEOS group of two Denon Home 200s, Tidal, FLAC 44.1/24 output, ICY off, crossfade off. Playback stopped near 434 s of a 466 s track and every Play retried that position and failed with HEOS 'Unable to play media'. An MA restart didn't help, skipping to the next track did. Incident log, diagnostics and a standalone repro attached.
cards.fix: server#7132 (draft): the flow route passes on whatever ffmpeg has encoded (read-any) when ICY is off, instead of waiting for a full second of encoded audio (~197 KB for FLAC). ICY framing unchanged. This restores the behaviour from before 4108ef5292 (Feb 2025, 'use static chunksize'); the single-item route already reads this way.
cards.checked: Opus subagent on origin/dev 03ee9a6872 (stable the same). The flow route reads ffmpeg output with chunk_size = icy_meta_interval if ICY else calculate_content_length(output_format) (controller.py:1546), via iter_chunked -> readexactly (helpers/ffmpeg.py:512/565, process.py:255-279), so for FLAC nothing is written until ~197 KB of encoded audio builds up. NEAR_REALTIME pacing only bursts 3 s ahead (streams/constants.py:100), so a quiet tail starves the player. Hermetic pytest repro: exact chunk size gives the first byte after 17.3 s on 20 s of silence, read-any under 3 s. ICY is off by default, so HEOS takes this path. Chunk size dates from 4bd03c2483 (Apr 2026). No fix PR.

cards.area: server / controllers/metadata _reconcile_duplicate_albums (candidate query) + single library DB connection
cards.summary: 2.10.5 HA add-on, huge library (58k artists, 64k albums, 284k tracks, 1117 playlists). The web UI hangs on every client because music/artists/count and other library commands never answer, while providers/players commands do. Nothing in the log, ~50% CPU. The hourly "Reconcile duplicate albums" task sat on "Searching for albums needing reconciliation" and had failed before with [Errno 2] on files under an old SMB share. Cancelling the task didn't help, a restart did.
cards.checked: Opus subagent, 2.10.5 = origin/dev on this path. All library queries share one aiosqlite connection with locking_mode=exclusive (music/database.py:187, helpers/database.py:246), so one long query blocks every count and library_items call. The slow-query warning only fires with PYTHONDEVMODE. Cancelling the task doesn't stop SQL already running on the connection thread (no interrupt()). The candidate query in _reconcile_duplicate_albums (metadata/controller.py:504, dev :610) uses _duplicate_album_sibling_guard: ORDER BY RANDOM() evaluates every album, each with an EXISTS over every other album with the same search_name. Same-title albums without a shared artist never short-circuit, so cost grows with the square of the biggest same-title group. #6236 removed exactly this pattern for tracks. Synthetic benchmark with the real dev schema and 64k albums: normal titles 0.03-0.18 s, 2000x "Greatest Hits" 1.1 s, 6000x 8.9 s. On HAOS with a 1.3 GB cache DB, minutes are plausible. Separate bug: FileNotFoundError isn't in the per-album error tuple (dev _SCAN_ITEM_ERRORS :100), so one missing file fails the whole run and the next hour runs the heavy query again. The diagnostics were taken 15 min after the restart, so they don't show the wedge.
cards.plan: Options: (1) cap the album candidate query like #6236 did for tracks (titles held by more than one provider, non-empty search_name, max 200 rows per title, or a CTE prefilter). My lean, plus (2) add OSError to the per-item error tuple. (3) Longer term: interrupt() watchdog or a separate read connection so maintenance queries can't block the UI, own design.

The opensubsonic parser stamps the artist cover_art thumb with provider=<instance id> and remotely_accessible=False. The flip: opening an artist runs music/refresh_item with overwrite=True, which replaces the stored images with the refreshing user's instance-stamped ones, so the other user loses them. Opening an artist runs refresh_item with overwrite=True from the viewer's own source, so the other account's images are dropped from the stored row and server#6708 has nothing usable left to pick for that user.

cards.summary: 2.10.6 HA add-on, Roku streaming stick on the AirPlay provider. Pausing and resuming skips 1-2 s of audio, and the progress bar jumps on pause. The reporter sent a Verbose log and diagnostics.

cards.checked: Opus subagent on the reporter's log (2.10.6) and airplay-cli origin/main a5a2175. cards.title: Sendspin→AirPlay bridge drops 1.7-3.3 s at stream start, and schedules each player at a different lead — a fixed, audible offset between RAOP players in one sync group
cards.summary: The dropped intro is real: on a realtime source (Spotify via soloist, YouTube Music, radio) Sendspin ignores the bridge's 4500 ms cold-start lead and schedules only min_buffer_ms (1000 ms) ahead, while the bridge can never anchor sooner than connect time + 2500 ms, so ~1.7-2.2 s is always cut on a cold start. The "per-player lead = audible offset" claim is disproved by the reporter's own log: the start_unix_ms gap (188 ms) equals the content-shift gap (2188-2000), so both players map the same sample to the same instant. The constant ~199 ms echo is device output latency, which is what sync_adjust is for. Code is identical between 2.10.3 and origin/dev.

lane: live
repro_cmd: worktree triage-6419 (origin/dev fd034e289) + cliairplay v0.5.4 in providers/airplay/bin; `ma-live.sh prepare`, set players.9056826F550E.values.preferred_output_protocol=spb_9056826f550e and players.ap9056826f550e.values.stored_volume=0 in the copy, `ma-live.sh start`, then `triage_logs/2026-09-27/repro/6419.sh <uri> 8` (not run: the pre-play volume guard failed)
evidence: No playback started. The caller's guard (volume 0 on the NAD AirPlay player and parent, abort if any NAD player reads above 5) can't be met. `players/cmd/volume_set` on ap9056826f550e/spb_9056826f550e is auto-resolved to the parent ("Auto-resolved protocol player spb_9056826f550e to linked parent 9056826F550E"), so over the API only the parent goes to 0. With the default config ap/spb read 400 (raw FALLBACK_VOLUME 20 under max_volume=5). With stored_volume=0 seeded, ap reads 0 but spb reads 500. Cause: `sendspin_bridge.py:438` `initial_volume=self.airplay_player.volume_level or 25`, where a 0 is falsy, so the bridge role starts at raw 25. `_enforce_volume_limits` then tries `_handle_cmd_volume_set(spb, 100)` (seen at registration, where it failed with "Player spb_9056826f550e is not available"). Under max_volume=5 every protocol-player reading is scaled x20, so any non-zero device volume reads >= 20. The literal "nothing above 5" guard can only hold at device volume 0.
unblock options (need a human decision): (a) guard on device scale instead (parent logical <= 5, ap/spb raw <= 5, no `VOLUME=` > 5 in run.log). The known worst case is a clamp push of VOLUME=5. cards.title: HEOS Integration plays announcements N times
cards.area: server / heos (player provider) + streams announcement URL
cards.summary: Repeated announcements on a HEOS speaker (Denon Home 150) play 1x, 2x, 3x. HEOS `browse/play_stream` appends to the device queue and starts playback at qid 1, MA's queue cleanup always keeps the "current" entry (so one stale MA entry survives every session) and the queue-connection `get_queue` is answered ~20s late, so cleanup never catches up. Every stale entry points at the same per-player `/announcement/{player_id}.mp3` URL, which serves the new announcement, so the device plays it once per queue entry; virtual repro goes red with `[1, 2, 3]`.
cards.fix: None. The fix means bringing back HEOS queue clearing (reworked before in #3932) and depends on real-device timing, or a controller-wide announcement URL change. This needs a decision with Tommatheussen. The plan is above.
cards.checked: A/B: A=n/a B=n/a A2=n/a
cards.plan:
Checked on origin/dev 3e1d945d0. `play_media` only calls `play_url` (`browse/play_stream`, which appends). `_cleanup_heos_queue` keeps `now_playing.queue_id` and runs only while `PLAYING`. The announcement URL is stable per player (`/announcement/{player_id}.{fmt}`). So the cause holds.

Why this isn't implemented unattended:
- Option 1 (keep the max qid and `player_play_queue` to it) does not fix the captured timeline on its own. `get_queue` on the queue connection answered after ~20s, which is after the next announcement's `play_stream`, so the "newest" qid is already stale when cleanup runs. A jump mid-announcement could also cut or restart the clip. Whether that is audible can only be checked on a real HEOS device.
- Option 2 (non-blocking `player_clear_queue` on the queue connection once MA playback reaches STOP) is the likely core fix. But it brings back queue clearing, which Tommatheussen reworked several times (ghost items, then #3932 because it blocked volume commands). Whether a clear on the secondary connection is fast enough, and doesn't race the next `play_stream`, is device behaviour we can't check here.
- Option 3 (a nonce per announcement in the URL, 404 on mismatch) is a controller change that affects every player provider. A maintainer should decide that.

Proposed direction, to agree with Tommatheussen:
1. HEOS: on transition to STOP/idle while `_ma_controls_playback`, schedule `player_clear_queue` on `_heos_queue` (fire-and-forget, logged on HeosError). Cancel it if a new `play_media` starts first.
2. HEOS: in `play_media`, if a clear is still in flight, await it (with a short timeout) before `play_url`, so the new stream lands on an empty queue at qid 1.
3. Keep `_cleanup_heos_queue` for multi-item flow sessions. Optionally switch it to keep the max qid.
4. Optional/separate: make announcement URLs unique per announcement (controller side), so stale queue entries on any player 404 instead of replaying the new clip.
Regression test: extend `tests/providers/heos/test_repro_6400.py` (fake device with delayed `get_queue`) to assert `[1, 1, 1]`.

cards.title: Universal Player config deleted at startup by a stale native link, recreated with a new id
cards.summary: After upgrading 2.10.2 to 2.10.6, a Juke Audio / Volumio AirPlay player wrapped in a Universal Player came back with a new player_id (upfc94fc52 became up56917d04). The native_claims loop (:349-367) treats any non-UP config whose stored linked_protocol_ids holds the UP's AirPlay id as the rightful owner, guarded only by _owns_domain_of_protocols (:511, #6610). It reparents the protocol to that native (:532) and deletes the UP config (:389-401) before the native registers. Root cause of the stale claim: _save_linked_protocol_ids (:1522-1540) only ever adds ids, so a native that once linked the AirPlay protocol keeps claiming it. #6610 (2.10.5) only covers a stale native that owns its own AirPlay protocol. cards.title: SiriusXM: sub-second dropouts every 10-40 s on AirPlay (RAOP)
cards.area: server / controllers/streams/audio.py HLS radio input (-stream_loop -1 -re) + siriusxm proxy (sxm 0.2.8 / aiosxm)
cards.summary: 2.10.6 HA add-on, Juke Audio zones over AirPlay RAOP. Every SiriusXM channel drops out for under a second every 10-40 s, alone or grouped. Spotify, local files and SomaFM on the same zones are fine. Tried buffer_depth 2000/3000 ms and enable_hires off; SiriusXM DEBUG logs show no errors. The 403 RetryErrors in the diagnostics were from two parallel streams, unrelated.
cards.checked: Opus subagent, code read on 2.10.6 and origin/dev plus a synthetic repro. HLS radio goes to ffmpeg with -stream_loop -1 -re and no burst (2.10.6 audio.py:4242-4250, dev :4915-4922), so ffmpeg keeps ~0.3-0.5 s lead. The HLS demuxer only fetches the next ~9.75 s segment at the end of the current one, and the SiriusXM proxy fetches it from the CDN on demand (sxm 0.2.8: precache loop is dead code, http.py:36 set_active misses nonlocal; dev aiosxm 0.3.0 stream.py:559-564 also per-request). Any boundary where reload + fetch exceeds the lead starves the player. Synthetic local HLS server with MA's exact args on ffmpeg 9.0.1: 0 ms delay no stalls; 700 ms delay gives a 0.70 s output stall per boundary with no errors; adding -readrate_initial_burst 10 absorbs it fully. Not tested on ffmpeg 7.1.2 (prod) or the real SXM CDN (no account). Side find: buffer_depth only applies to AirPlay 2 (airplay/stream.py:1138-1152), so the reporter's RAOP test changed nothing. No open PR.
cards.plan: Design call: (1, lean) add -readrate_initial_burst ~10 next to -re in the HLS radio branch, generic for every slow HLS origin, backport candidate; check ffmpeg 7.1.2 and the extra start/queue lag. Alternative: drop -re for HLS radio (riskier, it was added for the BBC stall). (2) Optional next-segment prefetch in aiosxm (MizterB). (3) Optional: skip the 5 s HLS metadata poll when the provider pushes metadata.
cards.reply:
> [!NOTE]
> This comment was written by Claude on Marvin's behalf

Thanks for the detailed report and for clearing up the 403s, that saved us a lot of time.

We think we found the cause on our side. For HLS radio like SiriusXM, Music Assistant reads the stream at exactly real time and keeps only about half a second of audio in reserve. SiriusXM delivers audio in roughly 10 second chunks, and each new chunk is only fetched when the previous one runs out. If that fetch takes longer than the reserve, you hear a short gap. That explains why the gaps are under a second, why they don't happen at every chunk, and why the logs show nothing. We reproduced the same pattern with a simulated slow stream, and a bigger read-ahead made it go away.

One side note: the AirPlay buffer_depth setting only applies to AirPlay 2, so on your RAOP zones those 2000/3000 ms tests didn't actually change anything. That's on us, not you.

We're working on a fix and will ping you here when there's a build to test.

cards.title: Sonos and Chromecast: manual next takes ~5 s before the new track is audible (Spotify via Soloist)
cards.area: server / controllers/player_queues (next debounce, queue_loader abort) + providers/spotify/soloist.py

A skip runs serially: fixed 1 s debounce (player_queues/controller.py:879-885), then play_index aborts the old buffer and awaits the producer (queue_loader.py:379-381, :1323, audio_buffer.py:415-418), which waits for Soloist to exit on SIGINT (soloist.py:332, :774, helpers/process.py:452). Soloist has one stream slot (spotify/provider.py:314), so the next track can't prefetch. A fresh --single-track daemon then logs in and delivers a first chunk (soloist.py:678, :706-715) before play_media goes out. Fake-daemon timing: AsyncProcess.close() adds no wait of its own, it lasts exactly as long as the daemon takes to exit. Estimated split: 1 s debounce + 1-2.5 s teardown + 1-1.5 s respawn + ~1 s player start. #4812 was AirPlay-only; server#6931 (2.11.0b5) fixes close() warnings, not the teardown time; #6873 covers speaker-side skips. Opus read of his DEBUG excerpts: the Sonos HEAD/GETs on the old session id are Sonos walking its cached cloud queue after the clean EOF, MA answers 404 (streams/controller.py:679-680), no delay from that. The quiet gap is MA work before play_media: _abort_superseded_source_buffers waits for the old Soloist run to stop (soloist.py:741-793, process.py:345-374), then get_stream_details, then a new --single-track daemon spawns, logs in and delivers a first chunk (soloist.py:361-423, 661-723), none of which logs. cards.title: AirPlay sync groups with 9+ members or after switching groups fail on PTP
cards.area: airplay-cli src/ap2_ptp.c (shared PTP daemon peer set)
cards.summary: On 2.10.7 (HA add-on, 57 players), AirPlay 2 sync groups go playing then idle, and one member logs that it has not answered the PTP clock. Groups with 9 or more AirPlay members always fail. A smaller group fails after a different group was used first, and works again after an MA restart or an AirPlay provider reload. The reporter's packet captures show the daemon sending Sync only to 7 or 8 peers, including a speaker from the previous group.
cards.checked: Confirmed in airplay-cli origin/main (1701bc2). The shared daemon peer set has a hard cap: PTP_MAX_PEERS 8 (src/ap2_ptp.c:102). peerset_add (ap2_ptp.c ~1700-1711) only appends and never reuses a slot whose refs dropped to 0. peerset_remove (~1713-1721) decrements refs but never frees the slot, so ps->n only grows. After 8 distinct receiver IPs have been registered over the daemon's lifetime, every new IP hits 'peer set full; ignoring'. The daemon lives as long as the provider (server providers/airplay/provider.py:827-863, --ptp-daemon), which is why a provider reload fixes it. A second leak is on the server side: stream.stop(force=True) (providers/airplay/stream.py:427) and _cleanup_failed_start (stream.py:1783) SIGKILL cliairplay. The 'U <ip>' unregister only runs in ap2_ptp_destroy (ap2_ptp.c:1237), so a killed stream leaves refs>0 and the old peer keeps getting Sync, matching the reporter's capture where Studio W still got Sync. Failed starts are killed, so one failure leaks more slots and the next start fails too. Followed HomePods (R ip F) also take a peer slot. No open airplay-cli PR or support issue covers this. I did not build the binary; this is from code reading, but it lines up with each step in the reporter's captures.
cards.plan: airplay-cli fix: make peerset_add reuse a refs==0 slot (or compact on remove), and raise PTP_MAX_PEERS to 16 or more. AP2_PTP_SHM_MAX_FOLLOW and AP2_PTP_SHM_VERSION are tied to it by a _Static_assert, so bump those together. Add a unit test for the add/remove/re-add cycle. Separately decide how the daemon drops peers whose cliairplay process was SIGKILLed, for example by tagging registrations with the client pid and reaping dead pids, or by sending SIGTERM before SIGKILL in stream.py.

cards.summary: Eversolo T8 and DMP-A6 using built-in Squeeze Connect drop and reconnect to MA's slimproto server about every 130 seconds, which interrupts playback. It starts right after the provider loads and while nothing plays, so it is not playback related. The T8 does not cycle in this log. aioslimproto (3.2.3 on stable, 3.3.0 on dev) sends strm 't' every 5 s (client.py _send_heartbeat, HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=5 in const.py). After each heartbeat it calls _render_display, which sends display/brightness frames unless the player reported a 0x0 display. The socket reader drops the client after 10 s of silence (client.py _socket_reader, timeout HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL*2). Nothing in the code gives a 130 s period, and the log is INFO only, so we can't see which side closes or why. One guess, not verified: the display frames sent every 5 s to a squeezeplay-type device with no display. The CLOSE-WAIT buildup points to a possible missed close in aioslimproto disconnect(), but I could not tie it to the cycle. 10-21: the three Verbose logs hold no aioslimproto lines at all. Log-level-only config changes skip the provider reload (models/provider.py:136), and the Squeezelite provider sets the aioslimproto logger level only in handle_async_init (squeezelite/provider.py:69-73), so it stayed at WARNING. The Verbose log and diagnostics it mentions are not attached, only a findings txt. In squeezeplay a ~130 ms reconnect comes from LocalPlayer connectToServer/connectIp (Comet serverstatus on 9000, a serv frame or discovery, DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT 120 s), not the slimproto read timeout (35 s, random 1-5 s backoff); confidence ~35%, Eversolo firmware is closed. Separate real bug: aioslimproto _socket_reader sets _connected False (client.py:652 in 3.2.3, :665 in 3.3.0) and then calls disconnect(), which returns early (:124), so write_eof/close never run and the socket sits in CLOSE-WAIT until GC. 10-21 15:30 (Verbose log + PCAP, TCP 3483 only): per session MA sends vers, setd, aude, audg, grfb, grfe; the T8 only SETD, then strm t every 5 s answered within ~2 ms; nothing left unanswered.
